mission: Ben considers and rejects a Jedi partner, instead calling Desh Rolan — establishing the Lie (self-reliance) through a control choice disguised as practicality
why_now: The mission requires a partner; Ben's choice of Desh over a Jedi reveals his trust architecture
conflict: Ben rationalizes choosing a non-Force-sensitive friend over a Jedi colleague as 'practical' — but it's actually about control and the danger of trusting Force-users after Jacen and Vestara
turning_point: Desh answers the comm with dry humor and agrees to the job without asking why Ben didn't call a Jedi. They both know why.
opening_hook: Ben scrolls past three qualified Jedi Knights on his contact list before his thumb stops on a name that isn't a Jedi at all
closing_hook: The wrongness in the Force shifts as Ben leaves Coruscant — not diminishing but acquiring direction, like a compass needle settling
emotional_trajectory: Calculated avoidance -> familiar comfort with Desh -> unsettled recognition that the wrongness is guiding him

stakes.personal: Ben's self-deception about why he chooses isolation over Jedi partnership
stakes.interpersonal: The Ben/Desh dynamic — friendship built on shared history neither discusses
stakes.external: The wrongness has a direction — it's pulling Ben somewhere specific

setting: Jedi Temple hangar bay -> comm call to Desh -> departure from Coruscant
sensory_details: Hangar echoes; Desh's voice tinny over long-range comm; hyperspace entry — the wrongness persists through hyperspace, which it shouldn't
promises_planted: Ben and Desh share unspoken GAG history (PP02)
Desh will matter to the climax (PP19)
notes: R01 lands at end of scene — the wrongness has a direction. This transforms Ben's departure from passive retreat to unconscious pursuit. Desh's arc starts here: lie_established — arrives as a favor, obligation not purpose.
